content: GPR75, also known as Probable G-protein coupled receptor 75, is a protein encoded by the GPR75 gene in humans. GPR75 belongs to the family of G-protein coupled receptors (GPCRs), which are cell surface receptors that activate guanine-nucleotide binding proteins (G-proteins) upon ligand binding. Currently, GPR75 is classified as an orphan GPCR, meaning its endogenous ligand has not yet been definitively identified. However, ongoing research is being conducted to determine its ligand. In one study, the chemokine CCL5 (also known as RANTES) was shown to stimulate calcium mobilization and inositol triphosphate (IP3) formation in cells transfected with GPR75. More recently, 20-hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acid (20-HETE), a bioactive eicosanoid produced via ω-hydroxylation of arachidonic acid, has been demonstrated to mediate its prohypertensive effects on the vasculature through activation of GPR75, specifically via Gq protein signaling pathways. This research, conducted by Dr. Schwartzman’s laboratory at New York Medical College, a leading group in the study of 20-HETE biology, has provided significant new insights into the pharmacology of GPR75.
